title: Pipes and plumbing
summary: The order system had a wild day and Brenda wants answers by lunch. Chain grep, cut, sort, uniq and head into pipelines that turn a 2000-line log into one-line answers.

nodes.hobnob: the order server, its log is /var/log/orders.log

tasks.title: How busy were we?
tasks.text: Each line of `/var/log/orders.log` is one order. How many orders came in yesterday?

tasks.title: How many went wrong?
hints: `grep 'status=failed' /var/log/orders.log` shows them. Too many to count by eye?
Pipe into `wc -l`, or use `grep -c`, which counts matching lines itself.

tasks.title: The nation's favourite
tasks.text: Which biscuit flavour (`cookie=...`) appears in the most orders? Submit just the flavour, for example `ginger-snap`.
hints: Step 1, pull out just the flavours: `grep -o 'cookie=[^ ]*' /var/log/orders.log`. (`-o` prints only the matching part; `[^ ]*` means "anything up to the next space".)
Step 2, count them: `uniq -c` counts runs of identical lines, but only if they are next to each other, so `sort` first: `... | sort | uniq -c`.
Step 3, biggest first: `... | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -1` (`-n` numeric, `-r` reverse).

answer_cmd.cmd: grep -o 'cookie=[^ ]*' /var/log/orders.log | cut -d= -f2 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -1 | awk '{print $2}'

tasks.title: The grumpiest customer
tasks.text: Customer support wants to send someone a free tin of apology biscuits. Which customer had the **most failed** orders?
hints: Same recipe as the flavour count, with one extra step at the front: keep only the failed orders first.

answer_cmd.cmd: grep 'status=failed' /var/log/orders.log | grep -o 'customer=[^ ]*' | cut -d= -f2 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -1 | awk '{print $2}'

tasks.title: Top three cities, on paper
tasks.text: Brenda wants the **three** cities with the most orders saved to `/root/top-cities.txt`, biggest first, one per line, in the format `uniq -c` prints: a count, then the city (for example `  381 leeds`).

checks.fail_msg: /root/top-cities.txt does not exist yet (or is empty).

checks.cmd: [ "$(grep -o 'city=[^ ]*' /var/log/orders.log | cut -d= -f2 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -3 | awk '{print $1, $2}')" = "$(awk '{sub(/^city=/, "", $2); print $1, $2}' /root/top-cities.txt)" ]
checks.fail_msg: The file does not hold exactly the top 3 cities with their counts, biggest first.

hints: Build the pipeline on screen first, and only redirect it to the file once the output looks right.
`grep -o 'city=[^ ]*' /var/log/orders.log | cut -d= -f2 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -3`. (`cut -d= -f2` keeps what comes after the `=`.)
`> /root/top-cities.txt` at the end of the pipeline sends its output into the file instead of the screen.

steps.cmd: grep -o 'city=[^ ]*' /var/log/orders.log | cut -d= -f2 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -3 > /root/top-cities.txt

tasks.title: Just the bad news
tasks.text: Run `bake-report`. It prints progress **and** errors, all mixed up on screen. Save **only the error lines** to `/root/errors.txt` (no progress lines in that file).

checks.fail_msg: /root/errors.txt does not exist yet (or is empty).
errors.txt should contain the 3 ERROR lines and nothing else.

hints: Try `bake-report > /dev/null`. Some lines still appear! A program has two output streams: **stdout** (1, normal output) and **stderr** (2, errors). `>` only redirects stdout.
`2>` redirects stream 2: `bake-report 2> /root/errors.txt`. (And `grep ERROR` would not help here: a pipe also carries only stdout.)
